definitions.explanation: Working the standard number of hours set by an employer, typically around 40 hours per week. Contrasts with part-time work.

examples.japanese: フルタイムで{働|はたら}いている。
{子育|こそだ}て{中|ちゅう}はフルタイムの{仕事|しごと}は{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: It's hard to work a full-time job while raising children.

examples.japanese: パートからフルタイムに{切|き}り{替|か}えたら、{給料|きゅうりょう}も{福利厚生|ふくりこうせい}も{良|よ}くなった。
examples.english: When I switched from part-time to full-time, both my salary and benefits improved.

notes:
A loanword from English "full-time." Used primarily in the context of employment to describe working standard hours, as opposed to パートタイム (part-time).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- フルタイムで{働|はたら}く: to work full-time
- フルタイムの{仕事|しごと}: a full-time job
- フルタイム{勤務|きんむ}: full-time employment
- フルタイム{社員|しゃいん}: full-time employee
- フルタイムの{主婦|しゅふ}: full-time housewife/homemaker

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {常勤|じょうきん}: full-time (employment) — more formal Japanese equivalent used in job postings and contracts
- パートタイム: part-time — the antonym, also a loanword
- {非常勤|ひじょうきん}: part-time, non-regular — formal antonym of {常勤|じょうきん}

USAGE:
フルタイムの{主婦|しゅふ} ("full-time housewife") is a common expression emphasizing that homemaking is a serious, full-time occupation. In sports contexts, フルタイム can also mean the full duration of a match.
